title: Article II · Of the things which are wholesomely and continually to be meditated and considered

blocks.s: Of the wise and virtuous man, already blessed in its beginning, it is said at the opening of the Psalms: His will is in the law of the Lord, and on his law he shall meditate day and night (Ps. i, 2). Hence elsewhere it is written: The things that God hath commanded thee, think on them always, and in many of his works be not curious (Ecclus. iii, 22, 24). This is what he did who sang and confesses: O how have I loved thy law, O Lord! it is my meditation all the day (Ps. cxviii, 97). Did not God also command this in Deuteronomy, saying: Thou shalt meditate on the book of this law, sitting in thy house, and walking on thy journey, sleeping and rising? (Deut. vi, 7). Elsewhere too the Scripture warns: Remember thy last end, and thou shalt never sin (Ecclus. vii, 40).

Further, we ought unceasingly and most diligently to attend to Christ fastened to the cross for us and as it were hanging on the cross, in every manner in which he hung there; and to his whole way of living in this world, his teachings and his exhortations, and to the way of living of the Saints in this life; but also we ought without ceasing to weigh the presence of the divine majesty, and how we may be able to please him, to answer him and to make satisfaction to him, and so in every virtue fittingly obtain an advance.
